newsitem.title: USA: Second former Texaco executive indicted.
newsitem.headline: Second former Texaco executive indicted.

text.p: Texaco Inc.'s former treasurer was indicted Friday for allegedly planning to destroy documents in a highly publicized race discrimination case, the second former Texaco executive to be charged in the scheme.
Robert Ulrich, the retired corporate treasurer, was indicted by a federal jury in White Plains, N.Y. on charges of conspiracy and obstruction of justice.
Richard Lundwall, former senior coordinator for personnel services in Texaco's finance department, was indicted in March for obstruction of justice in the same case.
The indictment issued Friday expanded the case against Lundwall, adding a count of conspiracy against him as well.
If convicted, both men face up to 15 years in prison.
The case against the men stems from Lundwall's decision to provide evidence against himself and his colleagues in the racial discrimination case brought by employees against Texaco.
In a lawsuit filed in 1994, a group of black employees alleged that Texaco discriminated against them in promotions and pay.
Lundwall had secretly taped conversations between himself and other Texaco managers in which they discussed destroying documents requested by the plaintiffs.
When Lundwall was dismissed by Texaco in a cost-cutting move last summer, he gave the tapes to the plaintiffs lawyers.
After the tapes were made public in court proceedings, Texaco agreed in November to settle the case for a record $176.1 million, according to plaintiffs attorneys.
The company also hired an outside investigator who provided Texaco with a report on what had happened at the recorded meetings. Texaco turned the report over to prosecutors.
